newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Monno Ceramic 1995/96 profit falls.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Monno Ceramic 1995/96 profit falls.

text.p: Bangladesh's Monno Ceramic Industry Ltd's net profit for 1995/96 fell 7.7 million taka to 41.5 million company officials said on Sunday.
The company, which makes tableware, is due to announce the year's result at its annual meeting on Monday.

The officials said the company would offer a 30 percent dividend to its shareholders for the year ended June 30. In 1994/95, the company paid the same dividend plus one bonus share for every two shares held.
Net profit declined in the year because of political trouble that seriously hit shipments, the officials said.

"Turnover also fell short of target due to troubles beyond our control. We had to charge depreciation and pay interest on bank financing for a 210 million taka modernisation and rehabilitaion programme in 1995," said Alamgir Mridha, the company's finance director.
However, turnover rose 71.65 million taka to 541.13 million in the year despite a drop in domestic sales.

Monno's tableware earned 363.1 million taka worth of foreign exchange through exports in 1995/96, up nearly 75 million from the previous year. In contrast, local sales dropped to 313.76 million taka from the previous year's 397.42 million.
"We are not facing competition in the local market. Overseas demands are rising (and) we are concentrating on the export market," managing director Harun-ur Rashid Khan told Reuters.
The United States is Monno's largest customer, buying 27 percent of its total exports. Other buyers include Britain, Italy, Spain, France, New Zealand, Australia, Holland and Argentina.
Khan said: "We are happy that we could offer our shareholders a 30 percent dividend despite all those political troubles."
Khan sees bright business prospect for his company, particularly overseas.
"We have tapped markets overseas. We have already proved very competitive both price-wise and quality-wise ... Monno is a name now at home and abroad," he said.
Khan claimed his company had not received any complaints from foreign buyers in the past 12 years. "There have been absolutely no complaints," he said.
Monno's tableware occupies the shelves of retail outlets such as Marks & Spencer Plc in the UK and Pier I Imports Inc in the United States.
Buoyed by the compay's export success, management is now considering a plan to produce top quality bone chinaware which requires 45 percent crushed animal bone as raw material.
"It's very much in our plan since we have got foreign markets," said Khan.
Monno Ceramic Industry Ltd started production in January 1985 and went public in the same year.
Its paid-up capital increased to 135 million taka in June 1996 from 90 million a year ago after the company offered 450,000 bonus shares at 100 taka each in 1994/95.
Monno Ceramic shares traded at 1,564 taka on the Dhaka Stock Exchange on Saturday.
